changes: Month 'तपस्थ' read as Tapasya (= Phālguna) and normalized; pakṣa 'सित' normalized to śukla
Year field left as the corrupt chronogram string, with a tentative analysis added in notes; still not resolved

notes: The colophon names no persons. The date line is a corrupt verse chronogram. It probably reads 'varṣe ṣaḍ-yugala-abhra-... gate māse tapasya-site'. Possible number words: ṣaṭ = 6, yugala = 2, abhra (for 'acchra') = 0. Read right to left, these give …026, and the last element ('nayad'?) cannot be identified, so the year and era are left unresolved. 'tapastha' is taken as Tapasya (Phālguna); 'site' = śukla pakṣa. Bendall gives no date conversion and calls the manuscript 'modern', so it is probably Nepāla Saṃvat, 19th century CE. This is not confirmed.
